noteRef.topicTitle: Structure and functions in living organisms

specPoints.text: describe the role of phloem in transporting sucrose and amino acids between the leaves and other parts of the plant

primer.text: Plants run two pipelines side by side. The xylem hoists water and minerals from root to tip through dead, lignin-strengthened tubes; the phloem ships sugary sap between source and sink through living cells. Same stem, opposite cargoes, opposite designs.

lessons.title: Two Pipelines, Two Cargoes
lessons.opening: The xylem transports water and mineral ions upward from the roots through hollow, lignin-reinforced tubes of dead cells, while the phloem ships sucrose and amino acids out of the leaves to wherever the plant needs them, through living tubes with sieve holes.
keyPoints: Xylem carries water and mineral ions from the roots upward.
Xylem vessels are dead, hollow cells stiffened with lignin.
Phloem transports sucrose and amino acids between sources and sinks.
Phloem tubes are living cells with small holes between them.
Together they form the transport system of vascular plants.

low.restatement: Xylem: up, water and minerals, dead stiff tubes. Phloem: sugars and amino acids, living tubes, either direction as needed.
low.analogy: A lift shaft that only goes up, next to a corridor where trolleys roll both ways.
low.examPointer: Name both cargoes precisely: sucrose and amino acids, not 'food'.

medium.restatement: The dead, reinforced xylem withstands the tension of the transpiration stream, while living phloem cells load and unload their cargo actively where it is made or needed.
medium.analogy: A chimney versus a conveyor belt with loaders: structure follows cargo.
medium.examPointer: Link lignin to strength-and-support in a structure-function sentence for full marks.

check.stem: What does the xylem transport, and from where to where?

options.text: Water and dissolved ions, upward from the roots
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.
Sucrose is the phloem's cargo.

options.text: Oxygen from the leaves to the roots
options.explanation: Oxygen diffuses; xylem sap is water and ions.
Amino acids ride the phloem in either direction.

check.stem: What fills a mature xylem vessel?

options.text: A hollow tube of dead cells with no cell contents
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.
Mature xylem cells are dead and empty.
That describes phloem architecture.
Starch sits in storage tissue, not xylem.

check.stem: Which material reinforces the xylem walls?

options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.
Cellulose is general wall material; the reinforcement named here is lignin.
Chitin builds fungal and insect structures, not plant vessels.
Keratin is an animal protein.

check.stem: Which substances travel in the phloem?

options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.
Those ride the xylem.
Gases move by diffusion, not phloem transport.
Both are insoluble storage and structural materials.

check.stem: Why does sucrose made in the leaves travel to other parts of the plant?

options.text: It is produced where photosynthesis runs and needed where growth or storage happens
options.explanation: Right — the other options each misplace a concept.
Leaves can store briefly; transport matches supply to demand.
Phloem flow is not gravity-driven.
The two systems simply carry different cargoes.

check.stem: State the roles of xylem and phloem in one sentence each.
check.modelAnswer: Xylem lifts water and dissolved mineral ions from root to shoot; phloem ships sucrose and amino acids from their source to wherever the plant needs them.

check.stem: Describe the structure of the phloem.
check.modelAnswer: Living cells join into tubes whose small sieve holes let substances pass.

check.stem: Explain why lignin reinforcement suits the xylem's function.
check.modelAnswer: The upward water column places the vessels under tension, and strong lignin-thickened walls stop them collapsing while letting the hollow bore stay open for flow.

check.stem: A ring of bark is removed from a trunk, cutting the phloem but leaving the xylem intact. Predict the effect.
check.modelAnswer: The xylem keeps water rising, so leaves stay supplied, but sugars can no longer pass the ring, so stores and roots below it starve while swellings form above the cut.

glossary.definition: The dead, lignin-stiffened vessels carrying water and minerals upward.
The living tubes transporting sucrose and amino acids around the plant.
The strengthening material impregnating xylem walls.
The movement of sugars through the phloem between source and sink.
